question: A paper about AI regulation that was originally submitted to arXiv.org in June 2022 shows a figure with three axes, where each axis has a label word at both ends. Which of these words is used to describe a type of society in a Physics and Society article submitted to arXiv.org on August 11, 2016?

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Task: Identify the June 2022 AI regulation paper’s three-axis labels from its figure (not just abstract), then find which of those words appears as a society type in a Physics and Society article submitted on Aug 11, 2016. history.content: Cross-match: from the figure we have possible words "Standardization, Localization, Hierarchical, Egality, Consequential, Deontological." Which of these appears in the 2016 Physics and Society abstract specifically describing a type of society?

history.content: The abstract explicitly describes "hierarchical" societies and "egalitarian" societies. I do not see "consequential," "deontological," or "standardization" as society types in the abstract. Among the set you listed, "Hierarchical" is present as a society descriptor.

history.name: Orchestrator

mistake_reason: At step 12, Assistant attempted to output structured axis labels in a JSON-like format but violated formatting rules (FM-4.4): used single quotes, included conversational preface before the structure, added a trailing comma, and left an unquoted token (source: arXiv:2207.01510). The malformed format caused parsing failure and introduced a semantic misread ("Egalitarianism" mis-OCR’d as "Egality" and an incorrect axis endpoint "Hierarchical"). Downstream agents relied on this flawed structure, selecting "hierarchical" as the match, yielding the wrong final answer.
